subject: general
question: Which of the following organisations or ministries released the report titled ‘India’s Services Sector: Insights from GVA Trends and State-Level Dynamics’ in October 2025?
solution:
p>The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The report titled **‘India’s Services Sector: Insights from GVA Trends and State-Level Dynamics’** was released by **NITI Aayog** in **October 2025** to provide a strategic roadmap for the tertiary sector.
 
• It focuses on the **Gross Value Added (GVA)** trends, highlighting how the services sector has become the primary engine of economic growth in India, contributing significantly to the national **GDP**.
 
• The report provides a detailed analysis of **state-level performance**, identifying top-performing states such as **Maharashtra**, **Karnataka**, and **Tamil Nadu** in terms of service output and innovation.
 
• One of the primary objectives of this publication is to address the **inter-state disparities** in service sector development and recommend policy measures to enhance **employment opportunities** and **export potential**.
 
• The document emphasizes the transition towards **knowledge-intensive services**, including **IT-BPM**, **Professional Services**, and **Financial Services**, which are pivotal for India's goal of becoming a **USD 5 trillion economy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India):**
 
 
• Established on **1st January 2015**, it replaced the erstwhile **Planning Commission** to foster **cooperative federalism**.
 
• The **Prime Minister** of India serves as the **Ex-officio Chairperson**, and it acts as the premier policy **Think Tank** of the Government of India.
 
• It focuses on long-term policy frameworks, monitoring and evaluation of government schemes, and promoting **innovation** through initiatives like the **Atal Innovation Mission (AIM)**.
 
 
 
• **Services Sector in India:**
 
 
• Commonly known as the **Tertiary Sector**, it encompasses a wide range of activities including **Trade, Hotels, Transport, Communication, and Financial services**.
 
• In the **Indian economy**, the services sector typically contributes over **50%** of the total **Gross Value Added (GVA)**, making it the largest contributor among the three sectors.
 
• India is a global leader in **software exports** and **Business Process Outsourcing (BPO)**, significantly boosting the country's **Foreign Exchange Reserves**.
 
 
 
• **Gross Value Added (GVA):**
 
 
• **GVA** is defined as the value of output minus the value of intermediate consumption. It provides a measure of the contribution to **GDP** made by an individual producer, industry, or sector.
 
• It is a crucial metric used by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** to track economic activity from the supply side.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Digital Transformation:** The report highlights that the **Digital India** mission has played a transformative role in enabling **contactless services** and expanding the reach of **e-commerce** and **fintech** across rural and urban landscapes.
 
• **Employment Generation:** While the sector contributes high GVA, the report points out the need for **skill development** to ensure that the workforce can meet the demands of emerging technologies like **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **Cloud Computing**.
 
• **FDI Inflows:** The **Computer Software and Hardware** and **Services** sectors consistently rank as the top recipients of **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** in India, showcasing global investor confidence.
 
• **Global Value Chains (GVCs):** **NITI Aayog** suggests that for India to improve its global standing, it must integrate more deeply into **Global Value Chains** by diversifying its service export basket beyond traditional IT services.

8f:T
